title: Prevent migraine attacks through targeted CGRP-pathway treatment

concept.text: Reduce migraine frequency with medicines developed against a validated migraine pathway. Erenumab established the approved preventive antibody class; treatment reduces attacks rather than constituting a permanent cure. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for adult migraine prevention, supported by randomized trials showing superiority to placebo in monthly migraine days over 3–6 months and in the proportion achieving at least a 50% reduction. Test set by: FDA; the pivotal protocols prespecified monthly migraine days and 50%-responder endpoints. Reported achieved: FDA approved erenumab (Aimovig) on 17 May 2018. Sources given: [FDA Aimovig approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761077Orig1s000Approv.pdf) ; [Aimovig prescribing information and trial outcomes](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=b998ed05-94b0-47fd-b28f-cddd1e128fd8&type=display).
